questions.q: Per Salesforce's object reference documentation, what effect does a lookup relationship have on deletion and security?
options: It cascades deletion to the child and controls its sharing, just like master-detail
It has no effect on deletion or security, and lookup fields aren't automatically required
It always deletes the parent when the child is deleted
It requires the child to inherit the parent's owner
questions.explain: The lesson quotes Salesforce's own documentation directly: a lookup relationship has no effect on deletion or security, unlike master-detail.

questions.q: A Contact can attend multiple Events, and an Event has multiple attending Contacts. Why can't this be modeled with a single lookup field on either object?
options: Because lookup fields can only be placed on standard objects
Because a lookup field holds exactly one value, and this is a many-to-many relationship, not one-to-many
Because Salesforce does not allow lookups between custom objects
Because Events cannot have child records
questions.explain: A lookup field can only point to one related record, so a true many-to-many relationship needs a junction object with two relationship fields instead.

questions.q: In the Event_Attendee__c junction object pattern, where should a 'Registration Date' field for a specific attendance live?
options: On the Event object
On the Contact object
On the junction object itself, since it's a property of that specific Event-Contact pairing, not either side alone
It cannot be stored anywhere in Salesforce
questions.explain: Data that only makes sense in the context of a specific pairing -- like a registration date for one attendance -- belongs on the junction object, not on either related object.

questions.q: Which relationship type is a special-purpose lookup available only on the User object, used to model management chains?
options: Master-detail relationship
Junction relationship
Hierarchical relationship
Self-relationship
questions.explain: The hierarchical relationship type is reserved for the User object's Manager field and related management-chain use cases, with its own sharing behaviors a generic self-lookup doesn't get automatically.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say relationship type is one of the hardest Salesforce data modeling decisions to reverse?
options: Because relationship types can be renamed but never deleted
Because once certain features (like a roll-up summary field on a master-detail relationship) are attached, Salesforce restricts converting that relationship to a different type
Because only System Administrators can view relationship fields
Because relationship design has no effect on deletion, ownership, or sharing
questions.explain: Salesforce's own documentation confirms that attaching a roll-up summary field to a master-detail relationship removes the ability to freely convert it to a lookup, which is exactly why this decision needs architectural forethought.
